Why this matters for SSC

India has 43 World Heritage Sites (as of 2025) — 35 cultural, 7 natural, and 1 mixed. SSC regularly asks 1–2 questions on the count, the first added, and 2–3 famous sites (Taj Mahal, Kaziranga, Sundarbans).

---

Natural7Kaziranga, Sundarbans, Western Ghats, Great Himalayan NP
Mixed1Khangchendzonga NP
Total43 (2025)1st: Agra Fort (1983); latest additions: Maratha Military Landscapes, Moidams (2024)
2024 additions: Maratha Military Landscapes of India (Cultural, 2024); Moidams of Charaideo (Cultural, 2024).
India is in the top 6 globally for number of WHS, behind Italy, China, Germany, France, Spain.

On India's Tentative List (not yet inscribed)

These are sites India has nominated; if/when inscribed, the WHS count will increase. Worth knowing:

  • Delhi's Imperial City (planned 2024 nomination)
  • Rani Durgavati Fort and Temple Complex (MP)
  • Sites of the Indus Valley Civilization (Dholavira already inscribed; Lothal, Rakhigarhi, Kalibangan, Banawali under review)
  • Varanasi (old city + ghats)
  • Satpura Tiger Reserve (MP)
India's Tentative List has 50+ sites. UNESCO considers one tentative list entry at a time.

Trivia for SSC

  • First Indian WHS: Agra Fort, 1983 (along with Ajanta Caves, Ellora Caves, Taj Mahal).
  • India's first mixed WHS: Khangchendzonga NP, 2016.
  • India's first natural WHS: Kaziranga, 1985.
  • First city WHS: Ahmedabad (2017); second: Jaipur (2019).
  • First intangible heritage on UNESCO list (India): Kutiyattam (Sanskrit theatre, 2001); followed by Vedic chanting, Ramlila, Mudiyettu, Kalbelia, Chhau dance, Buddhist chanting, etc.
  • Vatican City is the only WHS that is a country; Ethiopia is a country whose entire site is WHS (Lalibela, etc.).
  • India's 2024 additions (most recent): Maratha Military Landscapes (Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Goa) and Moidams of Charaideo (Assam). India now has 43 WHS.
  • India is in the Asia-Pacific region of UNESCO.
  • UNESCO HQ: Paris, France. Founded 1945.

  2. 2. Traditions of Vedic chanting — 2003
  3. 3. Ramlila (the traditional performance of Ramayana) — 2005
  4. 4. Mudiyettu (Kerala ritual theatre) — 2010
  5. 5. Kalbelia (folk songs and dance of Rajasthan) — 2010
  6. 6. Chhau dance — 2010
  7. 7. Buddhist chanting of Ladakh — 2012
  8. 8. Sankirtana (Manipur) — 2013
  9. 9. Traditional brass and copper craft of utensil making (Thatheras, Jandiala Guru, Punjab) — 2014
  10. 10. Yoga — 2016
  11. 11. Kumbh Mela — 2017
  12. 12. Durga Puja — 2021
  13. 13. Garba of Gujarat — 2023
  14. 14. Hindu calendar (Panchang) — 2023 (added in 2023)
Latest: Garba (2023), Hindu calendar/Panchang — added 2023. India has ~14 intangible heritage entries.

Key concepts

  • India: 43 WHS (35 cultural, 7 natural, 1 mixed) as of 2025.
  • 1983: first batch (Agra Fort, Ajanta, Ellora, Taj Mahal).
  • Kaziranga — one-horned rhino.
  • Sundarbans — mangrove + Royal Bengal Tiger.
  • Khangchendzonga — only mixed.
  • 2024 additions: Maratha Military Landscapes + Moidams.

2024–2025 Updates

  • 2024 (46th WHC, New Delhi, Jul 2024):
  • Maratha Military Landscapes of India — added to the Cultural list. Includes 12 forts spread across Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu: Raigad, Rajgad, Shivneri, Lohagad, Salher, Mulher, Rangana, Kasa, Sindhdurg, Panhala, Pratapgad, Suvarnadurg, Vijaydurg, Khanderi.
  • Moidams of Charaideo — added to the Cultural list. Burial mounds of the Ahom dynasty in Assam (Charaideo).
  • Total count: 43 WHS as of 2024 (35 cultural + 7 natural + 1 mixed).
  • No new inscription in 2025 (so far) — but India has 50+ sites on its Tentative List.
  • 46th WHC in 2024 was hosted in India (New Delhi) — first time India hosted the WHC.
  • Next inscription expected: Varanasi (Ghats of Varanasi) is a strong candidate; Hoysala (already inscribed 2023); Rakhigarhi (Indus Valley site) is on the Tentative List.
  • India in UNESCO ICH list (2024): 15 entries — Garba (2023) and Hindu calendar / Panchang almanac (2023) are the latest; Durga Puja (2021) and Kumbh Mela (2017) are earlier additions.
  • UNESCO HQ: Paris, France. Founded 1945.
SSC 2025 high-yield: Lock in 43 WHS, 2 new sites in 2024 = Maratha Military Landscapes + Moidams of Charaideo, and the first mixed WHS = Khangchendzonga (2016).
